Risk (what could go wrong): Staff enter passwords on a phishing page, giving an attacker mailbox access
Planned treatment: Require multi-factor sign-in for all mail accounts; phishing awareness session twice a year; report-this-email button

Risk (what could go wrong): No one knows who leads during an incident
Planned treatment: Adopt a written first-hour checklist; run a 30 minute tabletop each year

Risk (what could go wrong): Ransomware encrypts the shared file server before the tax deadline
Planned treatment: Keep one offline or immutable backup copy; test a restore each quarter; limit who can write to shared folders

Risk (what could go wrong): Laptop with client tax data is lost or stolen
Planned treatment: Full-disk encryption on every laptop; remote wipe; no local storage of client files

Risk (what could go wrong): Unpatched software on staff computers is exploited
Planned treatment: Turn on automatic updates; monthly report of machines more than 30 days behind

Risk (what could go wrong): Client data emailed to the wrong recipient
Planned treatment: Use the secure client portal for tax documents; delay-send on outgoing mail for 60 seconds

Risk (what could go wrong): No inventory of systems and cloud services in use
Planned treatment: Build a simple list of systems, owners and where client data lives; review twice a year

Risk (what could go wrong): Suspicious sign-ins go unnoticed for days
Planned treatment: Turn on sign-in alerts for unusual location; one person receives them

Risk (what could go wrong): IT provider has broad admin access and suffers its own breach
Planned treatment: Ask for the provider's security practices in writing; require separate admin accounts with multi-factor; put breach-notice time in the contract

Risk (what could go wrong): A departed employee's accounts stay active
Planned treatment: Same-day offboarding checklist; monthly list of active accounts compared to payroll

Risk (what could go wrong): Remote staff use personal devices without protection
Planned treatment: Written rule on personal devices; require screen lock and updates; prefer company laptops for client work

Risk (what could go wrong): Cyber insurance does not cover a payment-redirect fraud
Planned treatment: Read the policy exclusions with the broker; ask in writing about social engineering cover

Risk (what could go wrong): A key person is unavailable and nobody else can restore systems
Planned treatment: Document restore steps; store admin recovery details in a sealed offline envelope

Risk (what could go wrong): Guest Wi-Fi shares a network with office computers
Planned treatment: Separate guest network; change the router admin password
